assessment.headline: DAY 35. Oil surged the most in the entire war. UN blocked. India in coalition. Two days to the deadline.
assessment.body:
Today produced the single largest oil price surge of the entire war: Brent +7.8% to $109, WTI +11.4% to $111.54. The market has absorbed Trump's 'stone ages' speech and concluded: this war is intensifying, not ending.

The most alarming analysis comes from BCA Research (via CNBC): the world hits an 'oil cliff' in mid-April. The stopgap measures — strategic petroleum reserves, Russian oil sanction waivers, Iranian oil exemptions — all expire. Supply loss doubles from 5M to 10M barrels/day. 'There is no substitute for pumping oil from the ground and sending it directly to clients.'

The UN Security Council vote on Hormuz was postponed to Saturday after China, Russia AND France objected. Even if the watered-down version passes, enforcement is months away. Meanwhile Iran is drafting a permanent toll protocol with Oman — institutionalizing its control of the strait.

Overnight strikes: B1 bridge collapsed (8 dead, 95 wounded on Nature Day). Ballistic missile chief Atimi killed. Iran claims F-35 shot down (CENTCOM denies). Iran drones hit Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi refinery. Red Crescent warehouse struck in Bushehr. Hegseth fired Army Chief of Staff.

For India (Day 35, 7 PM):
• Markets CLOSED (Good Friday). Reopen Monday = April 6 deadline
• Brent $109. Indian basket likely above $120 now
• Foreign Sec Misri in 60+ nation Hormuz coalition talks
• India supplying fuel to Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka. Maldives requested
• 60 days stock. LPG 30+ days. Refineries >100%. 800 TMT cargoes secured
• Rupee 93.19 (RBI NDF ban holding)
• FII ₹1.23T outflow March. Manufacturing PMI 4-year low

The next 72 hours are the most consequential of the entire war:
• Saturday: UN votes on Hormuz (likely vetoed)
• Sunday: April 6 — power plant strike deadline expires
• Monday: Indian markets reopen into potential chaos

If April 6 passes without a deal, Trump has promised to hit power plants. Iran has promised 'permanent humiliation.' Oil could spike past $130 overnight. India must be prepared for the worst Monday in market history.
